html:
The Gazi Husrev-beg Mosque is the main mosque of Sarajevo, built in 1531 for Gazi Husrev-beg, the Ottoman governor of Bosnia who did most to make Sarajevo a city.

Husrev-beg paid for a madrasa, a public kitchen, baths, a library and a covered market around it, and Sarajevo grew from this core into the largest Ottoman city in the western Balkans. The mosque is the finest example of early Ottoman architecture in the region, designed by a leading architect of the Ottoman court. The madrasa and library still work. The mosque was damaged by shelling in the siege of Sarajevo in the 1990s and restored. It stands for the Muslim heritage of Bosnia.
sum: The Gazi Husrev-beg Mosque is the main mosque of Sarajevo, built in 1531 for Gazi Husrev-beg, the Ottoman governor of Bosnia who did most to make Sarajevo a city.
